title: Liquid Volume and Weight: Units and Tools
seo_title: Grade 3 Liquid Volume and Weight Worksheets: Units and Tools (TEKS 3.7D, 3.7E)
standard_text: 3.7D determine when it is appropriate to use measurements of liquid volume (capacity) or weight; 3.7E determine liquid volume (capacity) or weight using appropriate units and tools
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.7D and 3.7E: liquid volume or weight, customary and metric units, measuring cups and scales, reading containers and scales, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Liquid volume is how much a container holds. Weight is how heavy something is.
key_sub: Use a measuring cup for liquid volume and a scale for weight. Choose a unit that fits the size.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Liquid volume (capacity) tells how much a container holds. Use a measuring cup or a marked container.
  • Weight tells how heavy something is. Use a scale or a pan balance.
  • Customary units: cups, pints, quarts and gallons for liquid volume; ounces and pounds for weight.
  • Metric units: milliliters and liters for liquid volume; grams and kilograms for weight.

Examples

Example

Which unit is best for the water in a bathtub?

A bathtub holds a lot of water.

Cups and ounces are too small.

Answer: gallons (or liters)

Example

Which tool tells how heavy a pumpkin is?

Heavy means weight.

Weight is measured with a scale.

Answer: a scale

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using a scale to find how much a pitcher holdsHow much it holds is liquid volume: use a measuring cup.
Choosing a unit that is far too small or bigThink: is it like a spoonful, a cup, or a bathtub?
Reading the next number on a scaleCount the marks between the numbers to find what each mark is worth.

faq.a: Decide when it is appropriate to measure liquid volume (capacity) or weight.
Determine liquid volume or weight using appropriate units and tools, both customary (cups, quarts, gallons, ounces, pounds) and metric (milliliters, liters, grams, kilograms).

faq.q: What is the difference between liquid volume and weight?
faq.a: Liquid volume is how much a container holds. Weight is how heavy something is. A big balloon has a large volume but a small weight.

faq.q: How do you read a scale?
faq.a: Find the numbers on each side of the pointer, then count what each small mark is worth.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The left side is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the watermelon is heavier and the orange is lighter.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is lighter?
